should_fix.quote: carryover (the keys under "carryover:" ...) goes first, then SLOW ORDER's groups
should_fix.conflicts_with: A cap is never a hold: one you don't reach stays due as it is ... and goes first next run, ahead of its group's order
should_fix.scenario: SLOW ORDER's groups start with STEP 0 (feedback, bounces). A literal model works carryover follow-ups before STEP 0c's bounce scan and STEP 0b's feedback from Akshay, so a follow-up can go to an address that bounced since the last SLOW run, or against feedback not yet read. With a large carryover it can also eat the 40 minutes before STEP 0 (owner mail, scorecard) runs.
should_fix.fix: 'carryover goes first within STEP 2 (after STEP 0, STEP 1b and the team work); a carried key not in this run's eligible list is dropped.'

should_fix.quote: Stop only on the per-run or daily cap, the 40 minutes, or a tool error
should_fix.scenario: One transient error (a Blueticks read for a snooze, one Notion 504) ends the whole batch. That is safe, but it is the most likely early stop and it's undefined. A failed PRE-SEND check could also be misread as a 'tool error'.
should_fix.fix: 'a tool error: a connector call that fails after one retry; it stops only the work that needs that tool. A failed PRE-SEND check blocks that item only.'

should_fix.scenario: This can't collide with ACTIONS keys, because those start with the page id and never with 'snooze:'. But <its date> is '<D Mon>' (no year, has a space), and two snoozes on one row returning on the same date share one key. Processing twice is harmless ('A segment already rewritten is done').

A longer batch means more context per run. A crash before RELEASE leaves zoya-lock held, and every later hourly run (FAST replies included) skips until the CTO recovers it. Runtime is otherwise bounded: FAST stops new rows at 25 min, SLOW at 40 min from run start, release well before the next :38.
should_fix.fix: None to the text. On the first SLOW run, watch for 'lock release rejected' or a held lock.

checked_ok: Per-run cap: LIMITS 'this run's own sends' + FAST 'shared with your SLOW work' means FAST sends count. Cap 40/run (decision 317) and 150/day both bind, and both are named stop reasons, so ~97 due items cannot go in one run.

No cadence limit is lifted: the batch says 'within every limit there; no cadence changes'. The 7-day limit, ONE PERSON, ONE ASK (fresh read per mail), quiet hours, PR gap and nurture 10/run are per-item checks. D14 makes group limits defer, never 'stopped early'.

'a hold defers that one item only' doesn't weaken person-wide stops. No-contact ('stops all their rows'), Akshay's held decision and ONE PERSON are each evaluated per item from fresh reads, so the other items for that person hit the same stop. PRE-SEND checks are 'fresh at each send'.

Duplicate sends: a carryover item re-worked goes through ACTIONS' key-on-Activity lookup + Sent candidate check + idempotency_key = action key. Seq keys are stable (raised = step due date), so no resend.
PRE-SEND CHECKS, GUEST EXAMPLES, BOOKING LINKS are byte-identical in FAST and SLOW (shared SHARED list), including 'if any'. No contradiction.
verdict: ACCEPT. No blockers. Deploy pin then FAST as the handoff says. S1 worth a one-line fix at the next rebuild (or now if cheap).
